solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dropping ball in front of goal

indicators.note: one piece placed before another sets the order in which the two are written down

blocks.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O
a mission is an aim or goal to be achieved

explanation.surface: A footballer loses the ball just in front of the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' reads as a fumble in front of goal, but here it is a noun: the act of dropping, as a player is left out of a side.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is the act of leaving something out, so it is a noun for the leaving out of an item from a list or team.

clue.text: Charge forced down in case of sale

indicators.note: a case holds its contents, so the word for the case wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: tamped means packed or pressed down firmly
the case of sale is its outside letters

explanation.surface: Shoppers are made to pay up, or perhaps pushed down, at a bargain sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The case of 'sale' is just its outer letters, which wrap around the word for forced down.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush of animals or people, the same as a charge forward.

clue.text: Place to put butter that’s currently jammy

blocks.note: first meaning: literally spread on a bread roll
second meaning: enjoying a run of luck right now

explanation.surface: Breakfast talk: where the butter goes, and the jam too.
explanation.walkthrough: Jammy is British slang for lucky, which the breakfast surface disguises as jam on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone enjoying a sustained run of success, while literally a bread roll is where butter gets spread.

clue.text: A bit of heart shown by American, half victorious

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, with the rest dropped off the end

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
triumphant means having won

explanation.surface: A romantic gesture from an American who has only partly won.
explanation.walkthrough: Triumphant has ten letters, so its first five are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Each upper chamber of the heart is called an atrium, so it is one part of that organ.

clue.text: The compiler seen under a lot of riding gear for women

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter goes
in a down entry, a piece placed under another comes after it in the grid

blocks.note: riding a bicycle is biking
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The setter turns up beneath a heap of equestrian kit for female riders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding gear' looks like one phrase, but the split falls after riding; gear belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit, clothing worn mostly by women at the beach.

clue.text: Collapsed and woke in thong that’s tight

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: came to means regained consciousness
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone passed out and came round wearing an uncomfortably snug thong.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or project that collapsed has failed completely, producing no result at all.

clue.text: Maybe outcome of freezing asylum seeker’s wish

blocks.note: first meaning: physics, as liquid turns to solid
second meaning: a move to a different country

explanation.surface: A refugee left out in the cold hopes for a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags freezing as just one example of the physical process.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, water freezing into ice is a phase transition, while a refugee wants to move to another nation.

clue.text: Far from dear child being attracted by silver clothes

indicators.note: clothing covers a body, so this word wraps around the one before it

blocks.note: going for something means being drawn to it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A child far from a beloved parent is lured by money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a term of affection but means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear here means expensive; something sold very cheaply is said to be sold for almost nothing.

clue.text: Old vehicle with appealing appearance picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so we want a word that is pronounced like the clue words

blocks.note: good-looking, said aloud

explanation.surface: A vintage car with good looks catches the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The cab was named after its designer, Joseph Hansom.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom was a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab common in Victorian London.

clue.text: Protest one hour back inflamed complaint

indicators.note: back means the assembled string is read from right to left

blocks.note: a sit-in is a protest occupying a place
I is the Roman numeral one
hr is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: An hour-long demonstration ended up in an angry grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflamed' looks like angry, but it is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinitis is a medical condition in which the lining of the nose becomes swollen and irritated.

clue.text: Whizz and spin round

blocks.note: spin is public relations, PR
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Something rotating very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Whizz and spin both suggest rapid motion, but whizz is an expert and spin is press management.
explanation.definitionFit: A whizz is an expert, someone highly skilled, which is what a professional is.

clue.text: Instigate marketing inside stores the wrong way

indicators.note: stores means holds within, so the letters lie inside the run of text
the wrong way means the letters are to be read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of marketing and the start of inside

explanation.surface: A shop sets up its promotion back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to set something going, and one can start a row or a fire in the same sense.

clue.text: Spy author’s losing following, without 1000 followers

indicators.note: the abbreviation for following is dropped from the name
without here is old-fashioned for outside, so the name goes around the extra letter

blocks.note: Ian Fleming wrote the James Bond spy novels
f is the abbreviation for following, as in pages
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thriller writer loses fans though still has thousands of readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: These rodents are popularly believed to follow one another blindly off cliffs, so the term means unthinking imitators.

clue.text: As some say, mother’s ruin …

indicators.note: this points to how some people pronounce a word, so spelling follows speech

blocks.note: an informal word for mother, said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Mother's ruin is a nickname for gin, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: In accents that drop a final R, the word for ruin is spoken just like the familiar word for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it, the same as ruining it.

clue.text: We hear you must cut bigger loaf on this?

indicators.note: we hear points to a letter that sounds like the clue word
cutting into something puts a piece inside it

blocks.note: longer means of greater length
the letter U sounds like this word

explanation.surface: A baker asks whether a bigger loaf should be sliced on this board.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf is a verb, to laze around, not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining chair or sunbed, furniture designed for lazing about.

clue.text: … which comes from serving man before noon

definitions.note: refers back to mother's ruin in 13-down

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the other in the order

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier, a man in service
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: Mother's ruin comes from a servant before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 13-down: mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin, and 'which' stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit was blamed for wrecking families in eighteenth-century London, hence its old nickname.

clue.text: Good for Pierre, say, to eat egg or mushroom

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: bon is French for good; Pierre stands for any Frenchman
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A Frenchman enjoys an egg or a mushroom with his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg and mushroom look like foods, but both are verbs: egg is to urge and mushroom is to grow rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow or spread quickly, the same as to flourish and expand.

clue.text: Going against the flow, puts pants on early in the day

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rearranged as poor

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
re means on or about
am stands for morning

explanation.surface: A contrarian dresses at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but it is the British slang for rubbish; 'on' gives RE, as in regarding.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstream literally means moving opposite to a river's current, here used for the direction itself.

clue.text: Maybe like Dutch or Danish king, say, flipping frenzied!

indicators.note: flipping turns the preceding letters over, so they are read backwards

blocks.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
eg means for example, as say does
manic means wildly excited

explanation.surface: An angry outburst about a Danish monarch, perhaps Hamlet's father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish king' looks like a phrase, but Danish belongs to the definition and king is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: Both languages belong to the Germanic family, along with English and German.

clue.text: Those who oppose polluters save lake

indicators.note: save means except, so the letter named is left out

blocks.note: defilers are those who make something dirty
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Environmental protesters stand up to polluters to rescue a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like rescue but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: People who defy authority resist it openly, standing against its rules or commands.

clue.text: Desperate measure to introduce new form of ID

indicators.note: introducing a letter puts it into the word
desperate suggests wild and frantic, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Authorities take extreme steps to bring in a new kind of identity card.
explanation.definitionFit: A username is the login name that identifies a person to a computer system or website.

clue.text: Run sporty car, getting key in again

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the E-Type was a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: Driving a sports car and putting the ignition key back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a car key, but it means typing on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To key text in is to type it on a keyboard, and doing it a second time is retyping.

clue.text: Endless shock about formidable female

indicators.note: without an end, the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: to amaze is to astonish
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: An unending scandal surrounds an intimidating woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were a mythical race of women warriors, so the name is used for a strong, imposing woman.

clue.text: Hike round area on sierra — hurry after losing kit

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word wraps the letter
in an across entry, one piece on another comes after it

blocks.note: Sierra is the radio code word for S
a trek is a long walk
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A walker on a mountain range rushes home after losing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit here means clothes, as in British 'get your kit off'.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked through a public place, so it is a dash after shedding clothes.

clue.text: Paper bags I install

indicators.note: bagging something puts it inside a container

blocks.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper seizes an item that I put in.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit a kitchen or a part is to put it in place and set it up.

clue.text: Gently stuff in a kind of white meat

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play softly
Asti is a sparkling white wine from Italy
to ram is to cram or stuff

explanation.surface: Carefully filling some sort of white meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White meat' looks like one phrase, but white is a wine and meat stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured, smoked and spiced beef, often served sliced in sandwiches.

clue.text: Cause very grave offence, losing face

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so its first letter is lost

blocks.note: treason, betraying one's country, is among the gravest crimes

explanation.surface: A traitor's serious crime brings public humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the ground or motive behind something, the same as its cause.

clue.text: Seizing retired rugby player, international valuing tours

indicators.note: touring goes all round something, so this word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: ex means former
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
rating means assessing the worth of
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A retired rugby player is grabbed while a touring international team is being assessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expropriating means taking property from its owner, often by the state, which is confiscating it.
